alignments.note: Quantifier to *All*.

The ASV opens the verse asyndetically, writing no *but* or *now* for the connective. Variant SBLGNT.HEB.12.11.v005 is underdetermined and the projection carries r00-base; rule 12 forbids a new textual decision here, and the particle simply has no English word (rule 23).
`παιδεία` → *chastening*.
Preposition to *for*; the article takes its own *the* under rule 21.
Correlative `μέν` with the answering `δέ` at s015; the ASV writes no *indeed*, so rule 70 leaves it empty. The *yet* of t013 is the `δέ`'s own word and is not the correlation written here.
Substantival article before a participle; the ASV writes *the present*, so the article takes the determiner it brings (rules 21, 22) and the participle keeps its own word under rule 32.
Participle to *present*.
Ordinary negative to *not*; no negative indefinite stands, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Finite verb to *seemeth*, discontinuous from its complement under rule 15.
`χαρᾶς` rendered by the predicate adjective *joyous*.
Infinitive with its rule 7 marker; no conjunction governs the clause, so rule 40 does not apply and *to* stays with the verb (rule 61).
Adversative to *but*.
`λύπης` rendered by the predicate adjective *grievous*.
Adverb to *afterward*.
Connective to *yet*, which the ASV places before *afterward*.
`καρπόν` → *fruit* at t018; the second, italicized *fruit* at t028 is a repetition of this same word and is handled under rule 103.
Attributive adjective to *peaceable*; the noun is anarthrous in Greek and the ASV supplies no determiner, so rule 58 is not in question.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *them* and nothing else, with the dative's case preposition *unto* riding along under rule 21, as `τοῖς` → *to them* does at JHN.1.12.

Preposition fused with its governed pronoun into one English word: *there-* answers to `αὐτῆς` and *-by* to the instrumental `διά`, so rule 81 keeps the pair `aligned` and headed on the pronominal rather than reaching for `noncompositional` under rule 45.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and auxiliaries are rule 7 and 9 helpers on the participle, headed on the lexical verb *exercised*.
Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *yieldeth*.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*; rule 17 heads on the noun.

The ASV's supplied appositional *even*. Rule 105 folds such a word only onto an expressed preposition carrying the appositive, or leaves it `added` where a substantival article carries it; here neither stands — the appositive's own head noun is itself supplied English — so no source token licenses the word and rule 5 applies. Reading it as a helper on `δικαιοσύνης` remains defensible, but that word's English is already *of righteousness*.

Supplied repetition of the predicate noun: `καρπόν` (s016) is already spent on *fruit* at t018, so this second *the fruit* answers to no unspent source token and is `added` under rules 5 and 103, the supplied determiner staying inside the unit as GAL.3.20 and REV.4.1 keep theirs. Reading it as a discontinuous second realization of `καρπόν` under rule 15 remains defensible.

review_notes: Both `δέ` tokens differ: s015 has *yet* and is aligned; s002 opens the verse with no English word and is unrepresented. A reference comparison will flag s002 and the unwritten `μέν` (s005) as disagreements; under rules 23 and 70 those reports are not corrections.
s019+s020 → *thereby* is `aligned` and not `noncompositional`, per rule 81's unanimous corpus reading of the *there-*/*here-* portmanteaus.
The two `καρπός`-bearing English phrases were kept distinct: t018 realizes s016, and the italicized t027-t028 is the ASV's appositional repetition, `added` under rule 103.
